learning_outcomes.text: Define specific elements: stress tensor, principal stresses, secular equation, Cauchy equations, strain tensor, generalized Hooke's law, potential energy of volume change, potential energy of shape change, equivalent stress, failure theories.
Define stress and strain states in bodies.
Identify and utilize notions from fundamental sciences specific to the mechanical engineering domain.

Utilize basic concepts, theories, and models to explain and interpret theoretical and experimental results, working and assembly drawings, and phenomena and processes specific to mechanical engineering.
Use digital tools for presenting obtained results.
Possess the capacity for logical structuring, correct explanation and interpretation of results, and applying analysis methods and strength calculation.
Possess the capacity to investigate, design, and solve problems of dimensioning and verification of body structures under different loading states.

Develop professional projects using established principles and methods in mechanical engineering based on selecting, combining, and using knowledge, principles, and methods from basic sciences of the field.
Apply knowledge necessary for identifying and analyzing mechanical phenomena and understanding the effects produced on bodies by external actions.
Perform efficient work within a team and have the availability to self-regulate behavior in relation to others on an empathetic basis.
Respect ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks.
Integrate into the workgroup, apply effective relationship and work techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously inform and document oneself in one's field of activity by adequately using efficient learning methods and techniques.
Identify objectives to be achieved, available resources, work stages, and times.
Have an open, sincere, cooperative, receptive attitude of relationship and communication within the team.

syllabus_topics: Stress state at a point in a body. General (spatial) stress state. Plane and uniaxial stress state. Stress tensor. Variation of stresses around a point. Principal stresses, principal directions, secular equation, extreme tangential stresses, particular cases of stress state.

Strain state at a point in a body. General (spatial) strain state. Variation of strains around a point, principal strains, principal directions of the strain state. Particular cases of the strain state.
Fundamental equations of Elasticity Theory. Differential equilibrium equations (Cauchy). Geometric equations. Constitutive (physical) equations.

Potential deformation energy. Specific potential deformation energy. Elementary and total potential deformation energy. Specific potential deformation energy for spatial and plane stress states. Potential energy of volume change and shape change.
Failure (strength) theories. General considerations. Limit stress state, equivalent stress state, equivalent stress. Relations for calculating equivalent stress according to strength theories.

Stress state at a point in a body. Variation of stresses around a point. Determination of principal stresses and establishment of principal directions of stresses. Determination of extreme tangential stresses and slip directions. Lamé's ellipse and Mohr's circle.
Strain state at a point in a body. Determination of principal strains and principal directions.
Establishment of equivalent stresses according to classical strength theories.
Applications of elasticity theory to solving simple loading problems. Determination of the stress function (Airy) by the polynomial method for beams subjected to bending.
teaching_methods: Interactive lectures with demonstrations and descriptions using diagrams and equations written on the board
Presentation of calculation methods and relations
assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 5 is required for both the exam and the project activities. The final evaluation result is determined by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the course. Grades will be awarded on a scale from 1 to 10, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of minimum learning outcomes and the awarding of corresponding study credits.
